key_insight: Among four spray routes for WC-10Co-4Cr coatings on 304 stainless steel, HVAF and HVOF delivered the best overall wear performance, while HVAF gave the strongest corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: Choosing the spray process strongly changes coating density, hardness, tribology, and corrosion behavior, so process selection is as important as material composition for wear-critical, corrosion-exposed components.
method: Prepared WC-10Co-4Cr coatings on 304 stainless steel using APS, detonation spraying, HVOF, and HVAF.
Compared microstructure, Vickers hardness, wear rate/friction, and electrochemical corrosion performance across the four coatings.
Identified dominant wear mechanisms from wear-track morphology and particle load transfer behavior.
evidence_signal: Hardness increased from APS (771.4 HV) to DS (954.2 HV) to HVOF (1166.2 HV) and HVAF (1162.2 HV), while wear rate dropped from 7.93×10^-5 to 1.10×10^-5 mm3/N·m; HVAF also had the best corrosion metrics (Ecorr -0.37 VSCE, Icorr 1.75 μA/cm², Rp 20438.5 Ω).
watch_item: The results are based on a specific coating system, substrate, and test conditions, so the ranking may shift with different feedstock quality, thickness, or service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
